title: Clarify when to start a slice in agent workflows
lead: Agent guidance presents `next --start --show` as a one-call option while also requiring agents to inspect the slice and resolve ambiguity before starting work. State one clear sequence so efficiency guidance does not encourage premature status changes.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The current examples can leave agents unsure whether they should mark work started before validating its scope and acceptance criteria.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A focused assertion or review check confirms the standard flow reads the slice before marking it started.
2. Any documented `next --start` shortcut clearly identifies when it is appropriate and does not conflict with the spec-first flow.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Choose and document a single default sequence: fetch the next item and slice, inspect scope/dependencies/checks, resolve ambiguity, then start. Retain the combined start shortcut only with a clear precondition that the specification is already trusted. Keep descriptions consistent across quick start and detailed reference.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The quick start, reusable prompt, and detailed reference agree on when status changes, and a new agent can follow the workflow without choosing between contradictory examples.
